questions.question: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

Option 1) : ÷, -, +, ×, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 ÷ 17 - 54 + 18 × 6 = 56

⇒ 34 ÷ 17 - 54 + 18 × 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 54 + 18 × 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 54 + 108 = 56

⇒ 110 - 54 = 56

⇒ 56 = 56

LHS = RHS

Option 2) : ×, +, ÷,  -, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 × 17 + 54 ÷ 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 × 17 + 54 ÷ 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 × 17 + 3 - 6 = 56

⇒ 578 + 3 - 6 = 56

⇒ 581 - 6 = 56

⇒ 575 ≠ 56

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : +, ÷, ×, -, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 + 17 ÷ 54 × 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 + 17 ÷ 54 × 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 + 0.314 × 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 + 5.66 - 6 = 56

⇒ 39.66 - 6 = 56

⇒ 33.66 ≠ 56

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : ÷, -, ×, +, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 ÷ 17 - 54 × 18 + 6 = 56

⇒ 34 ÷ 17 - 54 × 18 + 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 54 × 18 + 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 972 + 6 = 56

⇒ 8 - 972 = 56

⇒ - 964 ≠ 56

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "÷, -, +, ×, =".

questions.question: By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct? 15 and 21
questions.questionHtml:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct?

15 and 21
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

Option 1) : 63 ÷ 15 + 21 × 5 - 4 = 74

After interchanging the number 15 and 21 in given equation the equation is as follows : 63 ÷ 21 + 15 × 5 - 4 = 74

⇒ 63 ÷ 21 + 15 × 5 - 4 = 74

⇒ 3 + 15 × 5 - 4 = 74

⇒ 3 + 75 - 4 = 74

⇒ 78 - 4 = 74

⇒ 74 = 74

LHS = RHS

Option 2) : 62 ÷ 31 - 21 + 15 × 3 = 80

After interchanging the number 15 and 21 in given equation the equation is as follows : 62 ÷ 31 - 15 + 21 × 3 = 80

⇒ 62 ÷ 31 - 15 + 21 × 3 = 80

⇒ 2 - 15 + 21 × 3 = 80

⇒ 2 - 15 + 63 = 80

⇒ 65 - 15 = 80

⇒ 50 ≠ 80

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : 24 - 21 ÷ 3 + 15 - 7 = 23

After interchanging the number 15 and 21 in given equation the equation is as follows : 24 - 15 ÷ 3 + 21 - 7 = 23

⇒ 24 - 15 ÷ 3 + 21 - 7 = 23

⇒ 24 - 5 + 21 - 7 = 23

⇒ 45 - 5 - 7 = 23

⇒ 45 - 12 = 23

⇒ 33 ≠ 23

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : 26 + 21 × 15 ÷ 3 - 14 = 108

After interchanging the number 15 and 21 in given equation the equation is as follows : 26 + 15 × 21 ÷ 3 - 14 = 108

⇒ 26 + 15 × 21 ÷ 3 - 14 = 108

⇒ 26 + 15 × 7 - 14 = 108

⇒ 26 + 105 - 14 = 108

⇒ 131 - 14 = 108

⇒ 117 ≠ 108

Hence, the correct answer is "63 ÷ 15 + 21 × 5 - 4 = 74".

questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years did the Ramsar convention to promote conservation and wise use of all wetlands through regional actions and international cooperation come to force in India?
questions.solution: The Ramsar Convention, an international treaty aimed at promoting the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands, was adopted globally in 1971. It came into force in India in 1982, marking the country's commitment to preserving its wetland ecosystems through regional and international collaboration. By joining the convention, India undertook measures to protect these vital habitats, which support biodiversity, regulate water cycles, and provide livelihoods for millions. This milestone highlighted India's proactive approach to environmental conservation on both national and global scales.

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly referred to as 'Ozone Hole'?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is commonly referred to as 'Ozone Hole'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Stratosphere.

Key Points

  • An ozone hole refers to a region in the stratosphere where the concentration of ozone becomes extremely low in certain months.
  • Ozone (chemically, a molecule of three oxygen atoms) is found mainly in the upper atmosphere, an area called the stratosphere, between 10 and 50 km from the earth's surface.
  • The cause of the formation of the hole is attributed to the unusual weather at the poles.
  • It is responsible for protecting life on Earth from the harmful UV radiation from the Sun.
  • The lack of the Ozone layer can have severe implications for people living directly under it. The most prominent effects are Skin Cancer and other possibly fatal skin diseases.

Additional Information

Layer Description
Troposphere

It contains most of our weather - clouds, rain, snow. In this part of the atmosphere, the temperature gets colder as the distance above the earth increases, by about 6.5°C per km.

The troposphere contains about 75% of all of the air in the atmosphere, and almost all of the water vapour (which forms clouds and rain).
Biosphere

The biosphere is defined as the region on, above, and below the Earth’s surface where life exists.

The biosphere is related to the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere, which are all spheres of the physical world.
Lithosphere The lithosphere is the outermost layer of Earth, composed of the crust and the brittle part of the upper mantle.

questions.question: The sides PQ and PR of ΔPQR are produced to points S and T, respectively. The bisectors of ∠SQR and ∠TRQ meet at point U. If ∠QUR = 69°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.questionHtml: The sides PQ and PR of ΔPQR are produced to points S and T, respectively. The bisectors of ∠SQR and ∠TRQ meet at point U. If ∠QUR = 69°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given, ∠QUR = 69°

If the bisectors of ∠SQR and ∠TRQ meet at point U

∠QUR = 90° - ∠P/2

⇒ ∠QUR = (180° - ∠P)/2

⇒ 69° = (180° - ∠P)/2

⇒ 180° - ∠P = 2 × 69° = 138°

⇒ ∠P = 180° - 138° = 42°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 42°

Alternate Method

Given:

∠QUR = 69°

Concept used:

The sum of all angles on a straight line is 180°

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°

Calculation:

∠PQR + ∠RQS = 180°

⇒ ∠RQS = 180° - ∠PQR

⇒ ∠RQS/2 = (180° - ∠PQR)/2

⇒ ∠RQS/2 = 90° - ∠PQR/2

⇒ ∠RQU = 90° - ∠PQR/2  [∵ QU is the bisector of ∠RQS]

Similarly, ∠QRU = 90° - ∠PRQ/2

In ΔQUR, ∠RQU + ∠QRU + ∠QUR = 180°

⇒ [90° - ∠PQR/2] + [90° - ∠PRQ/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ 180° - [∠PQR/2 + ∠PRQ/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ 180° - [(∠PQR + ∠PRQ)/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ 180° - [(180° - ∠P)/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ [(180° - ∠P)/2] = 69°

⇒ 180° - ∠P = 2 × 69° = 138°

⇒ ∠P = 180° - 138° = 42°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 42°

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 616 cm 2 and the area of its base is 38.5 cm 2 . What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the cylinder? (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 616 cm2 and the area of its base is 38.5 cm2. What is the volume (in cm3) of the cylinder? (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Given:

The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder = 616 cm2

The area of the base of the right circular cylinder = 38.5 cm2

Formula used:

The area of the base of a right circular cylinder = π × (radius)2

The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder = 2 × π × (radius) × (height)

The volume of a right circular cylinder = π × (radius)2 × (height)

Calculation:

Let, radius = R

So, π × R2 = 38.5

⇒ 22/7 × R2 = 77/2

⇒ R2 = (77/2) × (7/22) = 49/4   .....(1)

⇒ R = 7/2 cm

Also, 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × (Height) = 616

∴ Height = 616 × (1/2) × (7/22) × (2/7) = 28 cm

Then, the volume = (22/7) × (49/4) × (28) = 1078 cm3

∴ The volume (in cm3) of the cylinder is 1078 cm3

questions.question: An isosceles ΔMNP is inscribed in a circle. If MN = MP = \(16\sqrt{5}\) cm, and NP = 32 cm, what is the radius (in cm) of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: An isosceles ΔMNP is inscribed in a circle. If MN = MP = \(16\sqrt{5}\) cm, and NP = 32 cm, what is the radius (in cm) of the circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

MN = MP = 16√5 cm

NP = 32 cm

Formula used:

Area of a triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height

Circumradius = ABC/4Δ

Where. A, B, and C are three sides of the triangle

Δ = Area of the triangle

Calculation:

MD is perpendicular to NP

So, ND = DP = 32/2 = 16 cm

MD = √[(16√5)2 - (16)2] = √(1280 - 256) = √1024 = 32 cm

Area of ΔMNP = (1/2) × 32 × 32 = 512 cm2

Circumradius = (16√5 × 16√5 × 32)/(4 × 512) = 20 cm

∴ The radius (in cm) of the circle is 20 cm

questions.question: Let ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and \( \frac{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC})}{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{QPR})}=\frac{64}{169} \text { }\) If AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 16 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: Let ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and \( \frac{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC})}{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{QPR})}=\frac{64}{169} \text { }\) If AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 16 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR

ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔQPR) = 64/169

AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 16 cm

Concept used:

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the squares of the corresponding sides

Calculation:

ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔQPR) = AC2/PR2

⇒ 64/169 = 162/PR2

⇒ 8/13 = 16/PR

⇒ PR = (13 × 16)/8 = 26 cm

∴ PR (in cm) is equal to 26 cm

Mistake PointsΔABC ~ ΔPQR is important 

It does not matter what is given in the ratio form, 

That is \( \frac{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC})}{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{QPR})}\)

Hence we always solve the question according to ΔABC ~ ΔPQR.

questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought 40 pieces of an article at a rate of ₹50 per item. He sold 35 pieces with 20% profit. The remaining 5 pieces were found to be damaged and he sold them with 10% loss. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.solution:
The total cost price = 50 × 40 = ₹2000

The profit = \(\left[\left(\frac{100+20}{100}×50 \right)×35\right]+\left[\left(\frac{100-10}{100}×50 \right)×5\right]-2000\) ⇒ (60 × 35) + (45 × 5) - 2000 ⇒ 325

The profit% = (325/2000) × 100 = 16.25%

questions.question: Let x cm 2 be the surface area and y cm 3 be the volume of a sphere such that y = 14x. What is the radius (in cm) of the sphere?
questions.questionHtml: Let x cm<sup>2</sup> be the surface area and y cm<sup>3</sup> be the volume of a sphere such that y = 14x. What is the radius (in cm) of the sphere?
questions.solution:
Given:

The surface area of a sphere = x cm2

The volume of a sphere = y cm3

y = 14x

Formula used:

The surface area of a sphere = 4 × π × (radius)2

The volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × (radius)3

Calculation:

Let, radius = R

So, 4πR2 = x   .....(1)

Also, (4/3)πR3 = y

⇒ (4/3)πR3 = 14x  [∵ y = 14x]   .....(2)

Multiplying equation (1) by 14,

56πR2 = 14x   .....(3)

Justifying equations (2) and (3),

(4/3)πR3 = 56πR2

⇒ (4/3)R = 56

⇒ R = 42 cm

∴ The radius (in cm) of the sphere is 42 cm

questions.solution:
Let, total investment = 6 units

So, A invest = 6/3 = 2 unit, B invest = (6 - 2)/4 = 1unit, and C invest = 6 - (2 + 1) = 3 unit

Profit will be distributed in the ratio, A : B : C = 2 : 1 : 3

Here, 6 units → ₹186000, then 2 units → (186000/6) × 2 = ₹62000
